population_reference.methodology: OWID continental aggregates; UN World Population Prospects 2024. Historical estimates, not current-year projections. Antarctica is a separate permanent/seasonal-population observation.

europe.area_scope: Rounded geographic estimate, approximately 10.4 million square kilometres. Boundaries with Asia are conventional; this is not the sum of member countries' full areas.
europe.population_scope: OWID continental aggregate based on UN WPP 2024, reference year 2023. Whole-country statistical assignments differ from physical boundaries and the registry's multiple memberships. Not a 2026 census.
europe.highest_scope: Caucasus, Russia; uses the convention placing this summit in Europe.
europe.lowest_scope: Historical approximate shoreline reference from NASA photograph documentation, not the current lake level. The water level changes over time.
europe.river_scope: Conventional approximate river length; measurements depend on source and channel definitions.
europe.lake_scope: Approximate conventional surface-area reference for the shared European-Asian inland water body. Water level and area vary; Lake Ladoga is the largest lake wholly within Europe.

africa.area_scope: Approximate continental land-area reference including associated islands; geographic boundary conventions can differ.
africa.population_scope: OWID aggregate from UN WPP 2024 for 2023, using whole-country statistical assignments. This is not a sum of duplicate transcontinental registry entries or a 2026 census.
africa.highest_scope: Tanzania; elevation above mean sea level.
africa.lowest_scope: Djibouti; approximate surface/shoreline elevation below sea level, not lake-bottom depth.
africa.river_scope: Approximate National Geographic atlas reference. Source-selection methods produce different published lengths.
africa.lake_scope: Approximate atlas surface-area reference shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya. Published estimates differ by shoreline definition and water level.

asia.area_scope: Approximate physical-continent land-area reference. The Europe-Asia boundary is conventional and is not equivalent to whole-country statistical regions.
asia.population_scope: OWID continental aggregate from UN WPP 2024 for 2023. Whole-country statistical assignments differ from geographic boundaries; Russia is not split into a separate Asian population here.
asia.highest_scope: China-Nepal border; official snow-surface height announced in 2020, rather than rock-summit elevation.
asia.lowest_scope: Dated approximate shoreline level from the cited geological report. The Dead Sea continues to change; this is not a current observation or lake-bottom depth.
asia.river_scope: Conventional approximate main-system length; headwater selection changes reported measurements.
asia.lake_scope: Shared European-Asian inland water body. Approximate conventional surface area; level and shoreline change over time.

north-america.area_scope: Reference continental land area including associated islands. Central America, Greenland and the Caribbean belong to this broad grouping.
north-america.population_scope: OWID aggregate from UN WPP 2024 for 2023, using the broad North American grouping, not only the Northern America statistical subregion.
north-america.highest_scope: Alaska, United States; rounded metric equivalent of 20,310 feet. Both widely used mountain names are retained.
north-america.lowest_scope: Death Valley, United States; exposed land elevation, approximately 282 feet below sea level.
north-america.river_scope: Approximate combined length published by the National Park Service. Other headwater definitions yield different lengths; this is not the Mississippi alone.
north-america.lake_scope: Hydrologically connected single lake system. If Michigan and Huron are counted separately, Lake Superior is the largest named lake at approximately 82,100 square kilometres.

south-america.area_scope: Approximate continental land-area reference including associated islands. Boundaries and inland-water treatment can differ between sources.
south-america.population_scope: OWID aggregate from UN WPP 2024 for 2023. Whole-country statistical assignments are used, rather than repeatedly counting territory memberships.
south-america.highest_scope: Argentina; official mean-sea-level height announced by Instituto Geografico Nacional in 2012.
south-america.lowest_scope: Santa Cruz, Argentina; approximate surface elevation in the Gran Bajo de San Julian depression.
south-america.river_scope: Conventional approximate length. Alternative headwaters and estuary definitions yield different values, so global longest-river rankings are disputed.
south-america.lake_scope: Largest freshwater lake by surface area in South America under the conventional definition excluding coastal lagoons such as Maracaibo. Surface area varies with water level.

oceania.area_scope: Regional land-area reference including Australia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea and Pacific islands, excluding western New Guinea. This is not Pacific Ocean surface area.
oceania.population_scope: OWID aggregate from UN WPP 2024 for 2023. Statistical Oceania excludes Indonesia; it differs from a geological definition including all of New Guinea.
oceania.highest_scope: Physical Australasia including western New Guinea, Indonesia. This broader mountain convention differs from the area/population scope above; Mount Wilhelm is the highest in Papua New Guinea, while Kosciuszko is the mainland Australian high point.
oceania.lowest_scope: Australia; approximate lake-bed elevation below sea level, not the water level during a flood.
oceania.river_scope: Longest continuous Australian river system under Geoscience Australia's 2008 mapped-channel calculation. The Murray alone is about 2,508 kilometres.
oceania.lake_scope: Approximate maximum filled surface area of a usually dry or partly filled salt lake, not a permanent water surface.

antarctica.area_scope: Approximate continental area including permanent ice; excludes the seasonally expanding sea-ice cover. Published values vary with ice-shelf and coastline treatment.
antarctica.population_scope: Zero denotes no permanent native/resident population, not an uninhabited continent. Approximately 1,000 winter and 5,000 summer research/support personnel are a broad seasonal reference range, not a current station census. Density is not calculated from the permanent-population zero.
antarctica.highest_scope: Ellsworth Mountains; 2004 GPS measurement reported by USGS.
antarctica.lowest_scope: Approximate accessible surface/shoreline depression. This is not the continent's deepest subglacial bedrock, which lies much farther below sea level.
antarctica.river_scope: Approximate length of a seasonal surface meltwater stream, excluding subglacial drainage systems.
antarctica.lake_scope: Approximate subglacial lake area cited by USGS; the lake is beneath the ice sheet rather than an exposed water surface. Published geometric estimates vary.
